subject: history
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: What weakness in the League's main weapon of economic sanctions was exposed by the Abyssinia crisis?
options: Sanctions were illegal under the Covenant
Sanctions could only last one month
Members were forced to send armies
Key materials like oil were not effectively banned
questions.explain: During the Abyssinia crisis, sanctions failed because oil and the Suez Canal were not denied to Italy.

questions.q: Which British policy of giving in to Hitler's demands to avoid war is associated with Neville Chamberlain?
questions.explain: Chamberlain pursued a policy of appeasement, most notably at Munich in 1938.

questions.q: In which year was the League of Nations established, growing out of the post-war peace settlement?
questions.explain: The League of Nations was established in 1920, though agreed at the 1919 Paris peace conference.

questions.q: In which year did Hitler become Chancellor of Germany, beginning a more aggressive foreign policy?
questions.explain: Hitler became Chancellor in January 1933, after which he rearmed and challenged Versailles.

questions.q: The Nazi-Soviet Pact, agreeing not to attack one another, was signed in which year?
questions.explain: The Nazi-Soviet Pact of August 1939 secretly agreed to carve up Poland.

questions.q: After Munich, Hitler broke his promise by occupying the rest of which country in March 1939?
questions.explain: In March 1939 Hitler occupied the remainder of Czechoslovakia, ending British faith in appeasement.

questions.q: What did the secret clauses of the 1939 Nazi-Soviet Pact agree to do with Poland?
options: Divide it between Germany and the USSR
Hand it to the League of Nations
Make it a neutral buffer state
questions.explain: The secret protocol of the Nazi-Soviet Pact divided Poland between Germany and the Soviet Union.

questions.q: Which territory was taken from Germany and placed under League control for 15 years by the Treaty of Versailles?
questions.explain: The Saar coalfield was placed under League administration for 15 years before a 1935 plebiscite.

questions.q: Which major power refused to join the League of Nations, weakening it from the start?
questions.explain: The US Senate rejected membership, so the League lacked the world's strongest economy from the outset.

questions.q: Hitler's aim of expanding German territory to gain 'living space' in the east was known as what?
questions.explain: Lebensraum, or 'living space', was central to Hitler's aggressive eastern expansion plans.

questions.q: The League of Nations failed to stop which 1931 act of aggression in the Far East?
options: The German remilitarisation of the Rhineland
questions.explain: The Japanese invasion of Manchuria in 1931 exposed the League's weakness.

questions.q: At the 1938 Munich Agreement, which territory was handed over to Germany?
questions.explain: The Munich Agreement of 1938 gave Germany the Sudetenland region of Czechoslovakia.

questions.q: What military restriction did the Treaty of Versailles place on the size of the German army?
questions.explain: The German army was restricted to 100,000 men under the Treaty of Versailles.

questions.q: In which year did Hitler send troops to remilitarise the Rhineland in defiance of Versailles?
questions.explain: German troops remilitarised the Rhineland in 1936, with no Allied response.

questions.q: In which year did Italy under Mussolini invade Abyssinia, further undermining the League of Nations?
questions.explain: Italy invaded Abyssinia (Ethiopia) in 1935, a crisis the League failed to resolve.

questions.q: By the Treaty of Versailles, which industrial region of Germany was demilitarised?
questions.explain: The Rhineland was demilitarised under Versailles, a restriction Hitler defied in 1936.

questions.q: What name is given to Hitler's 1938 union of Germany and Austria?
questions.explain: The Anschluss of 1938 united Austria with Nazi Germany, breaching Versailles.

questions.q: What was the total figure eventually set for German reparations after the Treaty of Versailles?
questions.explain: Reparations were fixed at 6.6 billion pounds in 1921, a sum Germans deeply resented.

questions.q: Which prime minister returned from Munich in 1938 claiming to have secured 'peace for our time'?
questions.explain: Neville Chamberlain returned from the Munich Agreement declaring he had achieved 'peace for our time'.

questions.q: Which economic event of 1929 severely weakened the League of Nations' ability to act in the 1930s?
options: The Wall Street Crash and Depression
questions.explain: The Wall Street Crash of 1929 triggered a global Depression that fuelled aggression and weakened cooperation.

questions.q: In which year was the Treaty of Versailles signed, formally ending the First World War?
questions.explain: The Treaty of Versailles was signed in 1919, imposing harsh terms on Germany.

questions.q: The German invasion of which country in September 1939 directly triggered the Second World War?
questions.explain: Germany's invasion of Poland on 1 September 1939 led Britain and France to declare war.
